verification_level: FAST plus BATCH; STOP invoked on one unsafe safe-Rust API (rand::sys::atoi) and repaired, with the focused and full library suites and the adversarial probes run afterwards. No production unsafe expression was added.
scope: Per-file contract audit of the RAND entropy pool, provider seeding up-call, uniform/range draw, and Linux platform seam; the RC2 and RC4 block/stream ciphers; the RSA ASN.1 templates and the RSA backend bridge. All eight entries were the head of REMAINING-AUDIT.txt; none was deferred.

defects.description: The authority's ossl_rsa_dup tests `dupkey->pss->maskGenAlgorithm == NULL` (rsa_backend.c:543-544). RSA_PSS_PARAMS_dup deep-copies maskGenAlgorithm, so that half is false after a successful dup and the authority leaves the duplicate's maskHash NULL, which ossl_rsa_pss_get_param_unverified later reads through ossl_x509_algor_get_md(NULL) as SHA1. The transcription instead decoded dupkey->pss->maskGenAlgorithm and could refuse a key the authority accepts. It now implements the authority's literal condition, guarded so a NULL dupkey->pss is reported as a failure rather than dereferenced (the authority's NULL dereference is not reproduced). A new test pins the authority's NULL-maskHash consequence.

`pub(crate) fn atoi(s: *const c_char)` dereferenced a caller-supplied raw pointer from safe Rust, so a crate-internal safe caller could cause UB. It is now `pub(crate) unsafe fn atoi` with a `# Safety` contract requiring a NUL-terminated readable C string. Call sites in src/rand/unix.rs (2), src/rsa/pmeth.rs (1 direct), src/dh/pmeth.rs (1 direct) and the module's tests now carry SAFETY-noted unsafe blocks; the calls already inside existing unsafe blocks were unchanged. STOP invoked for this class.

rand_pool_grow was a safe fn taking *mut RandPool and forming &mut *pool, hiding a liveness/uniqueness obligation from its callers. It is now `unsafe fn` with the contract `pool` is live and this call holds its only reference. The three internal call sites carry SAFETY notes. No expression or layout changed.

defects.class: secret residue on a failure path
defects.description: ossl_rand_get_user_nonce allocated the nonce buffer with OPENSSL_malloc-equivalent and plainly freed it when EVP_RAND_generate failed, although that call may already have written nonce material. The owner is now OwnedBuf::new_cleansed_released at the authority's same allocation and release coordinates; the success path still transfers ownership with into_raw. Deliberate improvement over the authority's plain OPENSSL_free, not observable through the API.

The authority expands the RC2 key in key->data itself. This transcription used a stack [u8; 128] holding the caller's key bytes and the expanded schedule, and left it on the stack after return. The temporary is now cleansed (runtime::mem::cleanse) before it goes out of scope. Rc2Key remains caller-owned and is cleansed by its owner.

ossl_rand_pool_attach's documentation said attached buffers are never modified, but ossl_rand_pool_adin_mix_in XORs into pool->buffer for attached pools too. The attach note now says only that attached buffers are never freed, and adin_mix_in's # Safety requires the pool buffer (including an attached one) to be writable for pool.len bytes. No behaviour changes.

defects.class: secret residue on an error path
defects.description: fromdata_err, the authority's err: label, released d (the private exponent) with BN_free, matching rsa_backend.c's own label. On every arm that reaches it d never entered the key, so the value was left in freed storage. It is now BN_clear_free(d); n and e stay plainly freed because they are public. Deliberate improvement over the authority, not observable through the API.

documentation_corrections: src/rc2.rs RC2_set_key's contract now says a zero length underflows the expansion's last-byte index, which is what both implementations do, instead of claiming data[-1] is read.
src/rand/pool.rs's attach note no longer claims attached buffers are never modified, and adin_mix_in's contract names the writable buffer requirement.
src/rsa/backend.rs's ossl_rsa_dup note now states the authority's literal condition and the maskHash consequence instead of a condition the authority does not test.
retained_obligations: The RAND_POOL accessors and mutators take raw pointers and require a live pool; expressed in each unsafe fn's # Safety.
ossl_rand_pool_attach stores a caller buffer cast from *const to *mut; the caller must keep it alive and, if adin_mix_in is used, writable.
Rc2Key and Rc4Key schedules are caller-owned; the EVP cipher layer is responsible for cleansing them.
rand_uniform's per-draw entropy word is an uncleansed stack scalar, as in the authority.
The ASN.1 item callbacks receive borrowed raw pointers; the item machinery owns the lifetime.
ossl_rsa_fromdata/todata and the PSS 30 readers borrow the OSSL_PARAM descriptors and the RSA the caller supplies.
The provider dispatch and OSSL_PARAM descriptor contracts remain the callers' obligations.
contracts_reused: CRYPTO_* and secure-heap allocator seam at the authority's exact size/file/line
B19 BIGNUM cleansing (CBIGNUM_it, BN_clear_free on private components)
D351's rule that the authority's text, including its faults, is preserved unless it is undefined behaviour
RC-1 reference counting for the RSA key and the borrowed EVP_MD contexts
secret_bearing_buffers: src/rand/pool.rs RandPool.buffer: entropy. Cleansed and released by OwnedBuf::Drop (secure or plain clear-free) on ossl_rand_pool_free and rand_pool_grow; cleansed by ossl_rand_pool_reattach; handed to the caller by detach, whose cleanup functions cleanse. Attached buffers are neither freed nor cleansed (caller obligation).

src/rand/prov_seed.rs ossl_rand_get_user_nonce buffer: cleansed on the EVP_RAND_generate failure arm by OwnedBuf::new_cleansed_released (M71-D4) and handed to the caller on success; cleanup_user_nonce releases it through CRYPTO_clear_free.
src/rand/prov_seed.rs entropy and nonce pool buffers: handed out by detach and cleansed by ossl_rand_cleanup_entropy (secure clear-free) or ossl_rand_cleanup_nonce (clear-free).
src/rc2.rs RC2_set_key stack expansion: cleansed before scope exit (M71-D5). Rc2Key schedule is caller-owned.
src/rc4.rs Rc4Key schedule: written in place, no copy in this unit; caller-owned.

src/rsa/asn1.rs RSAPrivateKey d/p/q/dmp1/dmq1/iqmp and RSA_PRIME_INFO r/d/t use CBIGNUM_it, so the B19 BIGNUM destructor cleanses them. Test-only DER buffers are public-template or small test keys and are released by OwnedBlock.

src/rsa/backend.rs d (private exponent) is BN_clear_free'd on the pre-install error arm (M71-D7); duplicated private BNs are released through RSA_free's BN_clear_free fields; OwnedPrimeInfo releases through ossl_rsa_multip_info_free.
src/rand/rand_uniform.rs per-draw u32 entropy word: stack scalar, not cleansed (authority parity); no heap secret.

boundary_control.name: rsa::backend::tests::a_duplicated_pss_restriction_keeps_the_authoritys_null_mask_hash
boundary_control.reason: The M71-D1 repair restores the authority's condition, whose consequence is a NULL maskHash on the duplicate. The control builds a PSS-restricted key with an MGF1 identifier and asserts the duplicate retains maskGenAlgorithm while maskHash stays NULL; a regression to decoding dupkey->pss->maskGenAlgorithm fails the control (the decode refuses the NULL MGF1 parameter).

residuals: The eight files are audited, not SAFETY_DISCHARGED.
ossl_rsa_dup preserves the authority's maskHash consequence; later PSS reads of a duplicated key therefore use SHA1 for the MGF1 digest, as the authority does.
RAND_POOL's attached-buffer path writes through a const-cast buffer; the contract now states the writability requirement rather than reproducing the authority's unchecked write.
rand_uniform's entropy word is not cleansed; no constant-time claim is made.
RC2/Rc4 schedules are caller-owned and are not cleansed by these units.
